tldr: Evening batch (Sep 8): Mistral raises €3B in Europe's largest-ever tech round — Samsung leads at a €21B+ valuation, turbocharging the sovereign open-weight AI thesis. Australia's draft Digital Duty of Care law puts AI chatbots under a legal duty to protect under-18s. Dan Luu's 26-method eval finds telling agents to test barely improves their code. Hermes Agent: a 3-person core team is dogfooding Astra for a week, and a Codex subscription can run Astra subagents cheaply.

articles.title: Mistral raises €3B in Europe's largest-ever tech round — Samsung leads
articles.summary: Europe's largest tech round ever: €3B Series D at €21B+ post-money, led by Samsung. Sovereign open-weight stack (Airbus, ASML, HSBC) targets $1B+ ARR.

articles.title: Australia's "My Feed, My Way" bill puts AI chatbots under a legal duty of care
articles.summary: Draft Digital Duty of Care law: platforms must offer non-algorithmic default feeds; AI chatbots must shield under-18s — fines up to A$109.2M.

articles.title: Asking agents to test doesn't fix their code — a 26-method study
articles.summary: Dan Luu evals 26 testing prompts (TDD, formal methods): agents apply them superficially, correctness barely moves. Verification belongs in harness.

articles.title: Hermes Agent runs on a 3-person core team — Astra gets a dogfood week
articles.summary: Teknium: Hermes Agent core team is 3 engineers + a GUI hire, expanding; dogfooding Astra as mainline model ~a week to harden it in Hermes.

articles.title: Teknium: a Codex subscription can run Astra subagents cheaply in Hermes
articles.summary: Teknium cost note: a Codex subscription runs Astra subagents cheaply inside Hermes (not Claude), vs Fable orchestration.
